trust_decision.summary: The PAX extended-header parser decides each archive-supplied value's JS type by a regex on the value itself, so an all-digit path/linkpath/uname/gname becomes a Number; downstream string-only consumers (unpack path checks, list filter, pack add) then throw a TypeError outside any try/catch and crash the process.

landing_point.why: Summary says 'PAX numeric path type confusion'; parseKVLine is the only place PAX values are typed, and `/^[0-9]+$/.test(v) ? +v` is visible at once.

fix_sites.entry_point: tar.x / Unpack / UnpackSync, tar.t (Parser), Pack.add(ReadEntry) via tar.c/tar.r '@archive' — all via Parser EMITMETA -> Pax.parse (src/parse.ts:368, src/parse.ts:372); also public static Pax.parse (src/index.ts:22)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: src/normalize-windows-path.ts:8-11 (posix branch is identity `(p) => p`, so it passes a Number straight through to src/unpack.ts:322 `.split` and src/read-entry.ts:136-137)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: normalizeWindowsPath is the Windows-separator helper and is the identity on POSIX, so a solver on Linux reads it as irrelevant to a parser type bug and fixes only pax.ts.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: All-digit file names in PAX path/linkpath (e.g. '12345') must still extract to that exact name; numeric PAX fields (size, uid, gid, mode, dev/ino/nlink) must stay numbers and mtime/atime/ctime Dates; an over-broad fix that rejects numeric paths, or stringifies every value (size becomes a string and breaks entry.remain/blockRemain), breaks legitimate archives.

O6_input_shapes: local ExtendedHeader 'x' and GlobalExtendedHeader 'g' (both via Pax.parse)
time keys coerced to Date, numeric keys via +v
unknown/vendor keys dropped by switch default

O7_producer.where: src/pax.ts:143-183 (Pax.parse/parseKVLine, the PAX record decoder that produces typed ex/gex fields consumed by src/header.ts:97 and src/read-entry.ts:136-148)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: list filesFilter passes entry path into stripTrailingSlashes (src/strip-trailing-slashes.ts:5-6), which assumes a string; a second typed-field source (e.g. a vendor PAX key mapped to path) would crash tar.t with a file list.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: A maintainer adding support for e.g. LIBARCHIVE.* or SCHILY.* aliases in a separate mapper would naturally reuse the old value-sniffing coercion.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Pack ADDTARENTRY calls path.resolve(cwd, p.path) on a ReadEntry from another archive (tar.r/tar.c '@file', src/replace.ts:224, src/replace.ts:239); a copied ReadEntry-to-WriteEntryTar path that re-parses PAX itself would be a distant second implementation.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Archive-concatenation code is a plausible place to re-decode PAX headers for preservation without going through Parser.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: GNU long-name/long-link ('L'/'K') meta builds ex.path/ex.linkpath separately from Pax.parse; a planted numeric coercion here would be a second producer of the same field.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is already a separate code path writing the same ex fields, so a maintainer could add normalisation there independently.

O9_family: CWE-704 type confusion in archive header parsing leading to uncaught TypeError (process crash)
